dek: Mercury and Venus are both retrograde until Nov. 13. The sky over Scorpio season, from Halloween to the new moon.

slides.label: The double
slides.text: Venus has been retrograde since *Oct. 3*. Mercury joined it on *Oct. 24*. Love, money, texts and contracts are all under review until both turn direct on *Friday, Nov. 13*.

slides.label: The science
slides.text: Neither planet is reversing. The Farmers' Almanac calls it *apparent retrograde motion*, an *optical illusion*. Astrology reads it as review time: revisit, rethink, renegotiate, reconnect.

slides.label: The timeline
slides.text: Venus slipped back into Libra on Oct. 25 and goes direct at *7:27 p.m. ET* on Nov. 13. Mercury goes direct at *10:53 a.m. ET*, per Cafe Astrology. The Venus shadow lasts to *mid December*.

slides.label: Friday's square
slides.text: On Friday, Oct. 30, Mars squared retrograde Mercury, an aspect astrologers read as *friction*. Short tempers, sharp words, a debate that *should have been a DM*.

slides.label: This weekend
slides.text: Halloween night, the Moon sits in *Cancer* before entering *Leo at 12:18 a.m.* Sunday. Sunday's last quarter moon in Leo lands at *3:28 p.m.* Eastern, a release point, as clocks fall back.

slides.label: The rewind
slides.text: The *Hunter's Moon* peaked at 12:12 a.m. EDT on Oct. 26, and astrologers placed it in *Taurus*. Star Walk notes the Moon actually sat in the *constellation Aries*. Both can be true.

slides.label: Scorpio new moon
slides.text: The *new moon in Scorpio* arrives about 2:02 a.m. ET on *Monday, Nov. 9*, near 17 degrees Scorpio. With both planets still retrograde, astrologers read it as a *quiet intention*, not a launch.

slides.label: The Den's take
slides.text: A tool for reflection, not a fortune teller. Back up the phone, *reread the contract*, fix the website before the ads. Retrograde is the rehearsal. *Direct is opening night*.

cta_line: Write it down. *Don't post it yet.*

caption_instagram:
Venus and Mercury are both retrograde, and they turn direct on the same day: Friday, Nov. 13.

Venus, the planet of love, money and taste, has been retrograde since Oct. 3. Mercury, the planet of texts, contracts and commutes, joined on Oct. 24. AstroStyle called the double "akin to taking the medicine all in one gulp." On Friday, Mars squared retrograde Mercury, read as friction. Halloween night the Moon sits in Cancer before moving into Leo at 12:18 a.m. Sunday, and Sunday's last quarter moon in Leo lands at 3:28 p.m. Eastern as clocks fall back. Next up: the new moon in Scorpio around 2:02 a.m. ET on Monday, Nov. 9, which astrologers frame as a quiet intention, not a loud launch.

The other side: the Farmers' Almanac notes retrograde is apparent motion, an optical illusion. The Den reads the sky as a tool for reflection, not a prediction.

Whether or not you follow astrology, the retrograde frame is a useful operating habit.

Mercury and Venus are both retrograde until Friday, Nov. 13, per Cafe Astrology, AstroStyle and Synthesis Astrology. Astrologers read the window as a review period: revisit, rethink, renegotiate. Astronomers, as the Farmers' Almanac notes, call the backward motion an optical illusion.

At the Den, we are not pausing work for the planets. But a scheduled review window is good practice: back up the files, reread the contract, fix the website before putting money into ads, and return to the idea shelved in the spring. Then launch with a cleaner plan.

Do you build review periods into your calendar, or only fix things when they break?
